title: Scan hit on a gate
statement: Let $\tau$ be a task, let $n,iv,tv,B$ be natural numbers, let $w,E$ be finite bit strings, and let $o$ be an oracle. Suppose that every oracle query on the encoded unary string of length $n$ paired with the binary expansion of $q$ returns the bit of $E$ at position $q$, taking out-of-range bits to be $0$. Suppose also that the task target condition holds for the input encoding the unary string of length $n$ paired with $w$, that $|E|\le B$, and that the suffix of $E$ at position $p$ begins with $1$ followed by the encoding of a gate $g$ and a remainder. If $c\le B$ and $a\le B$, then the scan started in its gate-hit state with registers $(p,c,a)$ and no answer yet halts with every register bounded by $B$, answering true for a size task, answering whether the requested gate kind equals the kind of $g$ for a type task, and answering whether $iv$ is among the arguments of $g$ for an edge task.
hypotheses_covered: $n,w,E,o$ are respectively a natural number, bit string, bit string, and oracle
Oracle answers on encoded unary-length-$n$ inputs equal the corresponding bits of $E$, with out-of-range bits read as false
The target condition holds for the encoded unary-length-$n$ input paired with $w$ and indices $iv,tv$
$B$ is a natural number and $|E|\le B$
$p,c,a$ are natural numbers and the suffix of $E$ at $p$ is $1$ followed by the encoding of $g$ and a remainder
